Hi Alice,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really helpful to understand FintechCo's constraints and goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary from call:
- Primary goal: scale real-time fraud scoring for customer checkout (sub-100ms P50 inference)
- Expected volume: ~120M requests/month initially, spiking up to ~220M in Q4 (peak concurrency ~400 qps)
- Data residency: US-only, sensitive PII in request payloads (tokenization in-app)
- Security reqs: SOC2 and customer-specific audit logs; procurement will need evidence for SOC2 and data handling

Deployment modes we're considering:
- Hosted API: fastest to go-live, per-token pricing, good for initial pilots but may be costlier at scale
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools we can size to your qps with predictable monthly commit pricing (good fit if you want stable costs and private tenancy)
- Private (VPC/on-prem): for strict network isolation and full control — higher upfront setup and longer procurement

What we need from you to model costs accurately:
1) Typical payload size (avg tokens or bytes) for scoring requests
2) Percent of requests that are synchronous low-latency vs batch/retry windows
3) Any hard SLOs beyond the P50 <100ms (e.g., P95 targets)
4) Procurement timeline and whether finance prefers commit-based (monthly/annual) pricing or pay-as-you-go

Next steps I propose:
- If you can share payload size and a rough sync/batch split, I’ll loop in Aditya (cc'd) to produce a cost comparison: per-token Hosted vs Reserved Dedicated commit vs Private sizing estimate. I will attach a pricing model template for your team to review.
- We can schedule a 30-min follow-up to walk through the numbers and procurement questions — I suggested some times below.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-model.xlsx (template)

Thanks — I’ll aim to get a comparison back within 48 hours after we get the payload numbers.

Best,

Neha / Marissa — see attached CSV with the proposed cost breakdown and assumptions. High level summary below; I modeled both 12- and 36-month commits.

Assumptions (summary):
- Model: mid-sized LLM for scoring (optimized 8-bit quantized variant)
- Avg tokens per request: 150; avg generated tokens per req: 0 (predict-only)
- Target latency: P50 <100ms, P95 <300ms -> need dedicated low-latency routing + batching limits
- Concurrency sizing: baseline 300 qps continuous, reserve headroom for 450 qps spikes

Hosted (per-token estimate):
- At 120M req/mo: ~$0.012 per request (includes model compute + infra + margin) -> ~$1.44M/mo
- At 220M req/mo: ~$0.010 per request -> ~$2.2M/mo

Dedicated (reserved capacity):
- Suggested baseline: 6 GPUs (A100-class equivalent) with autoscale headroom to 8 for spikes; supports target latencies with constrained batching
- 12-month commit amortized cost: ~$420k/month (includes reserved infra, runtime, basic support)
- 36-month commit amortized cost: ~$360k/month
- Notes: Dedicated pricing assumes committed capacity and fixed instance pool; includes prefix caching and optimized kernels to meet latency SLOs

Private VPC / on-prem:
- One-time onboarding: ~$150k (setup, network integration, KMS/HSM integration)
- Monthly ops + infra (customer-managed or co-managed) depends on whether Redwood hosts infra; rough estimate: $500k+/month for fully customer-managed on-prem at your scale (we can tighten this after discovery)

Attachments: proposed_cost_breakdown.csv

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm if finance prefers the 12- or 36-month commit comparison and we’ll produce a formal quote with payment terms
2) If interested in Dedicated, we can schedule an SRE-level workshop to validate latency SLOs and sizing (30–45 min)
3) Provide SOC2 artifacts for procurement (I’ll upload the SOC2 attestation and vulnerability summary to the HubSpot deal and share a link)

Happy to jump on a call with Alice + Neha to walk through the numbers — I’m free Wed 17 Jun 9–11am PT.
